title: Hybrid life cycles
blurb: Define a hybrid life cycle, recognise one in a scenario and tell it apart from the extended life cycle.
question: A hospital is building a new outpatient wing to fixed architect's drawings, while the patient check-in software will be shaped by nurses' feedback every few weeks. What type of life cycle is this, and how would you define it?

teach.h: The best of both, in one project
teach.body: A hybrid life cycle is a life cycle that combines linear and iterative approaches within one project. In plain English: use a plan-first, step-by-step approach for the parts that are stable and well understood, and short feedback cycles for the parts that are uncertain or likely to change. It is still ONE project with one sponsor and one business case; it simply uses the right approach for each part.

steps.label: Concept
steps.sub: Linear: idea and outline business case

steps.label: Definition
steps.sub: Linear: agree the business case and baseline

steps.label: Iterative development
steps.sub: Time boxes: build, review with users, refine

teach.caption: Linear front and back end for governance; iterative in the middle where requirements emerge.

teach.h: Three ways to run a project

teach.body: The building has fixed drawings, planning consent and a construction contract, so it runs linear: Concept, Definition, Deployment, Transition. The self check-in kiosk software is different: nobody knows exactly what patients and nurses need, so it is built in two-week time boxes with nurse feedback after each. One project, one sponsor, one business case, two approaches. That is a hybrid life cycle.

teach.h: How the two strands run together
teach.caption: Illustrative timings. The software evolves in time boxes while the building follows its fixed plan.

teach.body: Choose a hybrid when part of the work is predictable and part is not: physical build plus software, or a fixed regulatory element plus user-facing features. It is also common when the organisation's governance wants a firm, linear business case and baseline before releasing funds, but delivery benefits from iterative feedback. The aim is control where it helps and flexibility where it helps.

rows.label: Short cycles throughout, users review each
Linear build, iterative software, one project
Continues after Transition until benefits arrive

teach.text: Don't confuse HYBRID with EXTENDED. Hybrid MIXES linear and iterative approaches. Extended ADDS phases (Adoption and Benefits realisation) after Transition. Exam distractors also invent names like 'combined' or 'reduced' life cycle: the APM term for a mix is hybrid.

items: Hybrid life cycle: combines linear and iterative approaches within one project.
Linear for stable, predictable work; iterative for uncertain, evolving work.
Typical patterns: linear Concept and Definition then iterative development, or linear build plus iterative software.
Still one project, one sponsor, one business case.
Hybrid mixes approaches; extended adds phases after Transition.

summary: You can now define a hybrid life cycle as the combination of linear and iterative approaches within one project. You can spot one in a scenario and explain why it differs from an extended life cycle.

A.q: Which of the following best defines a hybrid life cycle?
options: One that adds phases after Transition
One that mixes linear and iterative
One that repeats the linear phases
One that uses only time-boxed cycles
A.why: A hybrid life cycle combines linear and iterative approaches within one project.

whyNot.0: Adding phases after Transition describes the extended life cycle.
whyNot.2: Repeating linear phases is not a defined life cycle model.
whyNot.3: Using only time-boxed cycles describes an iterative life cycle.

A.q: A rail operator builds new platforms in a fixed sequence while its passenger information app is developed in sprints with user feedback. Which life cycle is the project using?
A.why: One project combining a linear strand (platforms) and an iterative strand (app) is a hybrid life cycle.

whyNot.0: The app work is iterative, so the project is not purely linear.
whyNot.1: The platform work follows a fixed sequence, so it is not purely iterative.
whyNot.2: Extended means adding phases after Transition, not mixing approaches.

A.q: In a hybrid life cycle, which kind of work is best suited to the linear element?
A.why: Linear working suits stable, well-defined work that can be planned in full before it is built.

whyNot.0: Features shaped by users suit the iterative element.
whyNot.2: Exploratory ideas need feedback cycles, so they suit the iterative element.
whyNot.3: Changing requirements suit iterative working, where scope can flex.

B.q:
Which TWO statements describe a hybrid life cycle?
1) It combines linear and iterative approaches
2) It adds Adoption and Benefits realisation
3) Different parts of one project can use different approaches
4) It can only be used on software projects
B.why: A hybrid combines linear and iterative approaches, so different parts of one project can be run differently.

whyNot.1: Adding Adoption and Benefits realisation describes the extended life cycle.
whyNot.2: Statement 2 describes the extended life cycle, and hybrids are not limited to software.
whyNot.3: Statement 3 is true, but hybrids are used on many kinds of project, not only software.

B.q: A project runs linear Concept and Definition phases to agree the business case and baseline, then delivers the solution in time boxes. What type of life cycle is this?
B.why: Linear early phases followed by iterative delivery is a classic hybrid pattern.

whyNot.0: Extended adds Adoption and Benefits realisation after Transition; nothing here is added at the end.
whyNot.1: Delivery in time boxes is iterative, so the project is not purely linear.
whyNot.3: The linear Concept and Definition phases mean it is not purely iterative.

B.q: Which of the following is NOT a sound reason to choose a hybrid life cycle?
options: Some work is stable, some is evolving
The board wants a firm business case
The team wants to avoid decision gates
A physical build includes new software
B.why: Hybrids don't remove governance: decision gates still control the project.

whyNot.0: Mixed certainty across the work is the main reason to choose a hybrid.
whyNot.1: A firm, linear business case and baseline alongside iterative delivery is a common hybrid driver.
whyNot.3: A predictable physical build plus evolving software is a typical hybrid.

C.q: How does a hybrid life cycle differ from an extended life cycle?
options: Both mix linear and iterative work
C.why: A hybrid MIXES linear and iterative approaches; an extended life cycle ADDS Adoption and Benefits realisation after Transition.

whyNot.3: Only the extended life cycle adds phases after Transition.

C.q: A board will only release funds against a fixed business case and baseline, but users cannot yet say what screens they need. Which approach best satisfies both?
C.why: A linear front end gives the board its business case and baseline; iterative development lets the screens emerge from user feedback.

whyNot.0: Fixing every screen early would force users to guess requirements they don't know yet.
whyNot.1: With no linear early phases, the board wouldn't get the firm business case it requires.
whyNot.2: Adding benefits phases after Transition doesn't solve the uncertain screen requirements.

C.q: Which phase sequence could describe a hybrid project?
C.why: Linear Concept and Definition, iterative time boxes, then a linear Transition combines both approaches.

whyNot.1: This is a pure linear life cycle.
whyNot.2: This is a pure iterative life cycle.
whyNot.3: These are the final phases of an extended life cycle, not a mix of approaches.

reteach.title: A kitchen refit with a smart-home twist
reteach.question: Your kitchen refit has fixed plans for the units and plumbing, but you want to try out the smart lighting and adjust it week by week. How is that a hybrid?

blocks.h: Two kinds of work, one refit
blocks.body: The units, worktops and plumbing are fixed: measured, ordered and fitted in a strict sequence. Changing your mind halfway would be expensive, so you plan it fully first. The smart lighting is different: you install a basic set-up, live with it for a week, then tweak scenes and colours. Same kitchen, same budget, same deadline, but two approaches. That mix is a hybrid.

blocks.text: It is still ONE project. A hybrid is not two separate projects running side by side.

explain.body: A hybrid life cycle combines linear and iterative approaches within one project. Learn that wording: the exam often asks you to complete it.

test.q: Which term does APM use for a life cycle that blends linear and iterative approaches within one project?
test.why: The APM term for a mix of linear and iterative approaches in one project is a hybrid life cycle.

whyNot.0: Agile is an iterative way of working, not the name for a mix of both.
whyNot.1: An extended life cycle adds Adoption and Benefits realisation after Transition.
whyNot.3: 'Adaptive' describes flexible, iterative working; it isn't the APM name for a mixed life cycle.

explain.body: Stable, well-understood work is planned fully and delivered in one sequential pass, such as a building, an installation or a fixed regulatory element.

test.q: In a hybrid project, which item most likely runs linear?
options: A website shaped by its users
A trial of new app features
test.why: A building to fixed drawings has stable requirements, so it suits the linear element.

whyNot.0: User-shaped work suits the iterative element.
whyNot.1: Trialling features is iterative by nature.

explain.body: Uncertain or evolving work is built in time boxes, reviewed with users and refined, with scope flexing within fixed time and cost.

test.q: Why is the iterative element of a hybrid used for evolving work?
options: It fixes scope at the very start
It removes the need for a sponsor
test.why: Iterative cycles let user feedback reshape priorities, which suits work whose requirements are still emerging.

whyNot.0: Iterative working depends on frequent user involvement.
whyNot.2: Fixing scope early is a linear feature.
whyNot.3: Every project needs a sponsor, whatever its life cycle.

explain.body: Hybrid answers 'HOW do we deliver?' by mixing approaches. Extended answers 'HOW LONG does the life cycle run?' by adding Adoption and Benefits realisation after Transition.

test.q: A colleague says 'our project is hybrid because it carries on after Transition to track benefits'. What is wrong?
options: That describes an extended life cycle
That describes an iterative life cycle
Benefits are tracked only in Concept
test.why: Continuing after Transition to realise benefits is the extended life cycle. Hybrid means mixing linear and iterative approaches.

whyNot.1: Iterative life cycles use time boxes; they aren't defined by tracking benefits after Transition.
whyNot.2: Benefits are realised mostly after handover, not in Concept.
whyNot.3: The colleague has confused hybrid with extended.
